newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SEBI seeks ways of reviving primary market.
newsitem.headline: India's SEBI seeks ways of reviving primary market.

text.p: India's market watchdog is considering a proposal to make blue-chip firms planning Euroissues to raise part of the funds locally to bolster a depressed domestic primary market starved of quality new issues, a top official said on Thursday.

"Generally, the talk going around is that the primary market is depressed because there are no good issues," said Vijay Ranjan, executive director at Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). "We're trying to see how we could revive it."
New debt and equity issues in August slumped to 3.63 billion rupees in August from 16.75 billion in July, figures compiled by Prime Database which tracks the primary market show.
India's top companies plan to raise $1.5-$2 billion through the issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs) over the next few months.

State Bank of India, the country's largest commercial bank, and Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd, the state-run overseas communications monopoly, top the list of issuers with plans to raise $400 million and $650-$800 million respectively.
SEBI does not regulate GDRs which is approved by the finance ministry.
Ranjan said the plan was fraught with some problems and SEBI would forward the proposal to the finance ministry for action only after it had the solutions.
It has not set a date for finalising this proposal.
Companies normally issue GDRs at a premium to their underlying Indian stock while domestic offering is always at a discount to the market price.
Ranjan said another proposal to boost the market was to allow companies to offer buy-back facility to investors in new equity issues. But this would need amending the statute, he said.
